identity.name: Russian Eastern Outskirts
alt_names: Government of the Russian Eastern Outskirts

predecessors.note: Semyonov had held Transbaikal under Kolchak's Russian State; the Russian State dossier ends in 1920.

successors.note: The Far Eastern Republic took Chita on 22 October 1920 and made it its capital.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 477,981 km2: the Transbaikal region around Chita. The page gives only "Territory at the time of its proclamation" and names the "Transbaikal" and the "Russian Far East"; no area. Cliopatria draws the land inside its Republics of the Soviet Union shape (1920-1921).

ledger.note: 1920, 16 January: "Grigory Semyonov announced in Chita the creation of the 'Government of the Russian Eastern Outskirts'" (infobox "Established: January 16 1920"). The page names the Transbaikal and gives no districts.

1920, 19 October: Red forces of the Far Eastern Republic begin advancing on Chita after the Japanese left it on 15 October; Semyonov passed his civil powers to a Provisional Eastern-Transbaikal Assembly in September. [Reviewer eu-17-x: source moved from the Far Eastern Republic page, which does not give these dates, to the Eastern Okraina page, which does.]

1920, 22 October: Chita falls to the Red forces; the regime, "left without territory, collapsed" and the Far Eastern Republic takes Transbaikal. [Reviewer eu-17-x: source moved from the Far Eastern Republic page, which does not give these dates, to the Eastern Okraina page, which does.]

1920, 22 October: fighting for Chita ends with its capture. [Reviewer eu-17-x: source moved from the Far Eastern Republic page, which does not give these dates, to the Eastern Okraina page, which does.]
1920, 28 October: "Disestablished: October 28" (infobox, no year shown); the page says the regime "left without territory, collapsed" at the end of October.

certainty.note: The page names no districts; the Transbaikal frontier is the Chita oblast of the Far Eastern Republic dossier.

sources.title: Eastern Okraina
sources.note: 16 January 1920 founded at Chita; Semyonov supported by the Japanese; "left without territory, collapsed" at the end of October; disestablished 28 October; the FER moves to Chita on 25 October.

sources.title: Far Eastern Republic
sources.note: 19 October 1920 advance on Chita after the Japanese left on 15 October; 22 October Chita falls.

notes: Short-lived (nine months, below the ten-year threshold) but the Far Eastern Republic dossier names it as a counterpart, so it is written. The territory is the Chita oblast; the page is silent on Amur and Primorye. The page says the FER government moved to Chita on 25 October and the infobox gives the end as 28 October, while the FER dossier dates the capture of Chita to 22 October; both are kept. The capital and the leader are the infobox's. The Russian State dossier (this batch) is the predecessor: the page does not say Semyonov accepted Kolchak's authority after November 1919. The Japanese occupation of Chita until 15 October 1920 is in the FER dossier's sources, not entered here as an occupation.
